title: Year 12 Biology Module 7 – Infectious Disease
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Biology Module 7, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What disease-causing agent is called a pathogen?
What transmission occurs through direct physical contact between hosts?
What transmission occurs through contaminated objects, food or water?
What organism carries a pathogen between hosts, such as a mosquito carrying malaria?
Which scientist developed postulates linking specific microorganisms to specific diseases?
Which scientist’s experiments helped disprove spontaneous generation and support germ theory?

categories.name: How does a plant or animal respond to infection?

questions.prompt: What waxy plant surface can act as a physical barrier to pathogens?
What plant pores can close to reduce pathogen entry?
What local animal response causes redness, heat, swelling and increased blood flow?
What process allows a white blood cell to engulf a pathogen?
What rise in body temperature can form part of an animal’s response to infection?
What term means the death of infected plant tissue around a pathogen to restrict its spread?
questions.answer: Hypersensitive response. Accept: localised cell death.

categories.name: How does the immune system respond to a pathogen?

questions.prompt: What non-specific defence system acts rapidly against many pathogens?
What specific defence system develops targeted responses and immune memory?
What foreign molecule is recognised by the immune system and can trigger a response?
What protein binds specifically to an antigen?
Which lymphocytes can differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
Which long-lived immune cells allow a faster response after later exposure to the same pathogen?

categories.name: How can infectious disease spread be controlled?

questions.prompt: What everyday practice such as handwashing helps prevent disease transmission?
What procedure separates potentially infected individuals to limit disease spread?
What preventive treatment exposes the immune system to antigens to produce immune memory?
What medicines are used to treat bacterial infections?
What medicines act against viruses?
What population-level protection occurs when enough people are immune to reduce transmission?

finalRound.prompt: What cells remain after an adaptive immune response and allow a faster response to later exposure to the same pathogen?
